previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old male with a history of COPD, interstitial lung disease, systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, lung cancer after radiation therapy, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for a three-day history of worsening shortness of breath, dry cough, and orthopnea. He denied fever, chest pain radiation, or lower extremity edema. Initial evaluation showed elevated BNP and chronic interstitial lung changes on imaging without acute pulmonary edema. He was treated for a COPD exacerbation with azithromycin, prednisone, and nebulizer treatments, leading to rapid improvement in respiratory status. His blood glucose was elevated, prompting a temporary adjustment in insulin regimen with increased glargine doses. He remained stable, ambulated independently, and was discharged home after two days with a plan to complete antibiotics and steroids, resume baseline medications, and follow up with pulmonology, primary care, and cardiology. Tobacco cessation support was encouraged.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year-old man with past medical 
history of non-ischemic systolic heart failure (EF 35%), ILD, 
CKD, DM, HTN, Afib on anticoagulation, AAA repair, COPD, recent 
diagnosis of lung cancer who presented for orthopnea x 2 days, 
in addition to some mildly worsened shortness of breath. He 
initially was started on prednisone and azithromycin for a 
possible COPD exacerbation, but since his physical exam was 
significant for lack of wheezing, he was diuresed for a more 
likely CHF exacerbation/mild volume overload. His medical 
problems were managed as follows: 

#Orthopnea: Improved with diuresis, though he was consistently 
net negative less than 1 L TBB. Orthopnea most likely occurred 
___ mild volume overload (h/o sCHF with EF of 35% - CXR with 
mild interstitial pulmonary edema) that he tolerates poorly 
given his significant pulmonary pathology including COPD, ILD, 
and cancer. proBNP 1890 which is elevated compared to his 
baseline of 600s during previous admissions. His home torsemide 
of 40 mg is increased to 60 mg, which he tolerated well for one 
day prior to discharge. His weight on discharge is: 94 kg. He 
will follow-up with Dr. ___ care. 

#Systolic congestive heart failure: Per last TTE in ___, 
patient has an LVEF of 35%. Symptoms improved with diuresis in 
the ED, but his orthopnea persisted. He was diuresed with IV 
lasix until he was no longer requiring O2. To optimize his CHF 
regimen, he was also started on 2.5 mg of lisinopril. He started 
an increased torsemide dosage of 60 mg one day prior to 
discharge, and was able to lie flat with significant improvement 
of breathing prior to discharge. 

#COPD - discussed smoking cessation with patient; he is 
unmotivated to quit. On ambulation, he maintained sats >90 on RA 
and does not qualify for home oxygen. He continued to receive 
albuterol and ipratropium nebs and was on O2 as needed to 
maintain sats of ~90%. 

#Abdominal Pain: Acute pathology was ruled out by abdominal CT 
and his pain appeared to be chronic in nature, most likely from 
constipation. Patient reported hard stools and infrequent bowel 
movements and abdominal pain improved slightly after BM. He 
continued to receive his bowel regimen during hospitalization. 
 
#Atrial Fibrillation: Patient remained in atrial fibrillation, 
and continued to take metoprolol for warfarin. He was also 
systemically anti coagulated with warfarin with a discharge INR 
of 2.6. Per wife, patient will follow-up at ___'s office on 
___ for follow-up/monitoring. 

#Hyperlipidemia  - continued to receive atorvastatin  
# DMII: Last A1c 8.1% in ___. Patient remained on home 
glargine, standing homalog, supplemented by sliding scale. 
#Lung Cancer: s/p cyberknife. Patient continues to smoke and 
despite several conversations on smoking cessation, stated that 
he would continue to do so. He will pursue outpatient oncology 
follow-up.  
#Depression w/ psychotic features vs schizoaffective disorder: 
Stable throughout hospitalization, continued on home regimen
#CKD (baseline 1.8-2.3): patient did not receive nephrotoxic 
medications and his Cr stayed within his baseline.
